newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening mixed, slipping later.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening mixed, slipping later.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to open a bit higher in mixed trade but continue Monday's decline later in the session. * Traders said the firmer dollar may boost interest-sensitives.
Toronto stocks were expected to opened a little higher in mixed trade on Tuesday but continue Monday's decline later in the session, traders said.
"I think at the end of the day we're going to be down. We may open up a little mixed higher... but I think the trend is still lower," one trader said.
He said eyes will continue to be on corporate results.

"(There were) no tremendous earnings out overnight, although Nortel didn't do badly, and BCE also last night didn't do badly, but I don't think it's enough to overcome what's going on in the U.S. and overseas this morning," he added.

Northern Telecom Ltd's first quarter earnings rose to US$0.41 from US$0.32 in the same period a year earlier, while BC Telecom's per share earnings climbed to C$0.52 in the first quarter from C$0.45 in 1996.
The trader said the financial services sector may be one bright spot in the market.
"The banks, the interest-sensitives may do all right with the dollar firming a little here," he said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange key 300 Composite Index dipped 28.62 points on Monday to close at 5797.65.
Canada's unadjusted March consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in the month and 2.0 percent in the year.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Sears Canada Inc reported an unexpectedly small first-quarter loss on Monday, and said retail revenues could grow by 8.6 percent or more in 1997.
* Nortel and BC Telecom were expected to react to earnings.
